recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-11098 in the current FHIR core build; future edits to Task.restriction should be handled under newer Task issues rather than this DSTU2 rename clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-11098 was a Published FHIR-core Task change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2. It requested clarification of the confusing Task.fulfillment element; the final resolution was to rename Task.fulfillment to Task.restriction and clarify that the children restrict fulfillment of the request pointed to by the Task.
initial_application: The requested change was applied by git commit 839bf586d6c1cf9a322e122852f0cc49bcfed263, a 2016 workflow batch commit whose message explicitly includes {#11098}. That commit renamed Task.fulfillment, Task.fulfillment.repetitions, Task.fulfillment.period, and Task.fulfillment.recipients to Task.restriction, Task.restriction.repetitions, Task.restriction.period, and Task.restriction.recipient, and added the request-fulfillment limitation definition.
additional_context: Task remains an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini, and the source has since moved from spreadsheet input to source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml. Later Published Task issues FHIR-31900 and FHIR-34136 refined the same area by adding a Task.restriction invariant and usage notes, clarifying restriction.period, and adding Task.requestedPeriod for stand-alone Task timing; these later changes preserve the FHIR-11098 rename/clarification.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml has no Task.fulfillment path or element, defines Task.restriction with the requested request-fulfillment wording, includes a usage comment limiting it to fulfillment of request resources, and carries the later invariant requiring a fulfill Task with a focus Reference.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 clarification added the Task.restriction invariant, usage note, and period clarification, confirming the current source's stricter interpretation.
Published R5 enhancement added Task.requestedPeriod and distinguished stand-alone Task timing from Task.restriction.period.
